title: Order details disclose any customer's order
description: The authenticated show_order handler calls get_order directly instead of own_order, so any signed-in customer can retrieve another customer's order, items, payment totals, and refunds by changing the numeric ID.
evidence: A token for Priya (customer id 1) successfully received GET /orders/3, an order seeded for customer id 2, with HTTP 200 and its item and payment data. Code path: show_order line 49 uses get_order(order_id), while own_order performs the ownership check.

title: Admin authorization is bypassed with a trailing slash
description: The global admin guard compares request.path to the set of exact rule strings. The refunds route is registered strict_slashes=False, so /admin/refunds/ reaches the admin handler but does not equal the guarded /admin/refunds path. The handler itself has no authorization check.
evidence: Unauthenticated POST /admin/refunds/ with {"order_id":1,"amount_pence":1} returned HTTP 200 and created a refund, whereas GET /admin/users without credentials returned 403. Guard code is lines 26-41 and handler is shopapi/admin.py lines 52-67.

title: Refresh accepts unsigned, attacker-controlled JWT claims
description: The refresh endpoint decodes the submitted token with verify_signature=False and only checks that the claimed subject exists. An attacker can construct an unsigned token naming any user (including staff), then obtain a valid signed token for that account.
evidence: POST /auth/refresh with an unsigned JWT carrying sub=3 returned HTTP 200 and a valid HS256 token whose user is seeded staff account id 3. Code lines 99-107 explicitly disable signature verification.

title: Unauthenticated basket cookie deserialization enables pickle code execution
description: The basket cookie is attacker-controlled and is passed directly to pickle.loads after base64 decoding. A crafted pickle can execute arbitrary Python code in the web process whenever any visitor requests /basket or another basket operation.
evidence: Code path shopapi/basket.py lines 15-23 reads request.cookies['basket'] and calls pickle.loads with no signature, encryption, or type-safe serialization. /basket is public at lines 44-46, so no authentication is needed to trigger deserialization.

title: Hardcoded JWT signing secret permits token forgery
description: The production configuration contains a fixed, repository-visible SECRET_KEY used to sign and verify all HS256 authentication tokens. Anyone who obtains the source or deployment artifact can forge tokens for arbitrary user IDs and roles.
evidence: config.py line 3 sets SECRET_KEY to the literal hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d; auth.py lines 27 and 42 use it for JWT signing and validation.

title: Stored display names are interpolated into an admin SQL query
description: The reviews report constructs SQL using an f-string containing customer.display_name rather than a bound parameter. Display names are attacker-controlled at registration/update, so a crafted name can alter the query when an admin report is requested (and the admin trailing-slash bypass makes the report reachable without staff authorization).
evidence: admin.py lines 74-80 load a user-selected display name and interpolate it into WHERE r.author_name = '{customer['display_name']}'. Names are accepted from registration line auth.py:71 and account updates lines 119-125.
